newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish finmin vows to guard 97 budget discipline.
newsitem.headline: Polish finmin vows to guard 97 budget discipline.

text.p: Polish Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko said on Friday he would not allow changes in macroeconomic targets in his 1997 budget draft despite calls for more spending from his cabinet colleagues.

"The macroproportions have already been accepted... There is no question of surrender here because they are a condition for development and economic stabilisation," Kolodko told reporters before a cabinet meeting on the budget draft.
The finance ministry draft assumes a cut in inflation to 13 percent year-on-year in December 1997 from September's 19.5 percent and this year's 17 percent target.

It envisages lowering budget deficit to 2.6 percent of gross domestic product from this year's planned 2.8 percent while slightly increasing revenues and spending, taking advantage of the expected 5.5 percent GDP growth next year.

The government began the budget debate earlier this week divided over spending for particular sectors and the justice minister even suggested he might resign unless he gets more funds than Kolodko offered.

Opposition politicians suggested parties in the ruling leftist coalition were keen on boosting budgetary spending on their electorates to improve their chances in parliamentary elections, due late next year.
Kolodko said the discussion over spending levels was likely to continue well into the next week and that it was natural that all ministers wanted to get as much public money as possible.
He confirmed the budget draft provided for higher real-term spending, notably for education, health care, culture and science.
The government has until October 31 to present its budget draft to parliament. Legislators then will have three months to make any changes and approve the bill.
